purpose: Teach: 佑/ケイ/オイラ/毎度/意地/過ち/泡/お出かけ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の家族写真、佑のうちと、ケイの家、並んでたな。
lines.en: Old family photos — Yu's house and Kei's, hung right beside each other.
lines.style: Soft, gazing backward in time. Slow pace, gentle weight on each memory. Voice settles into the past tense like sitting down into a familiar chair. Slight pause before the final detail, as if seeing the image clearly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 当時、私たちは「オイラとあんた」みたいに呼び合ってた。
lines.en: Back then, we used to call each other 'oira and anata'—like we were something else entirely.
lines.style: Warm chuckle under the breath. Voice brightens on the old nicknames, almost playful. A little shake of the head—the fondness of remembering something you'd nearly forgotten. Trailing softly into the meaning of it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 毎度、近所の集まりが、賑やかでね。
lines.en: Every neighborhood gathering was packed with noise and life back then.
lines.style: Gentle, almost wistful sigh on the opening. Voice carries the weight of time passed. Medium pace, lingering on 'packed with noise' like he can still hear it. Slight fadeout, like drifting back into the moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 意地を張った若い日々、思い出すわ。
lines.en: Those stubborn, headstrong days when we were young—I remember them all.
lines.style: Tender but matter-of-fact. No performance in the softness. Voice rests on 'stubborn' with quiet recognition. Gentle exhale toward the end, like closing an old album carefully. Steady, unhurried.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 過ちもあったが、二人で乗り越えた。
lines.en: We made mistakes, but we carried each other through them.
lines.style: Measured and clear, with quiet conviction. Light emphasis on 'carried'—not heavy-handed, just steady. Voice holds firm but warm. The cadence is solid, grounded. No doubt in the past tense.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: シャンパンの泡、結婚式、覚えてる?
lines.en: The champagne bubbles at our wedding—you remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Brighten on the memory. Voice lifts slightly, almost playful. The question at the end is gentle, inviting—not testing, but reaching. Warm and intimate, the kind of voice that expects an answer you both already know.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 明日、温泉にお出かけしようか。
lines.en: Shall we go to an onsen tomorrow?
lines.style: Open, almost bright. Voice shifts forward into the present, into possibility. A gentle invitation rather than a plan. Slight upward lilt on the question, warm and easy—the voice of someone comfortable suggesting something simple and good.
